result.question: How many marriages were contracted in 2023, 2024 and 2025 combined where the older spouse lived in Norway?
result.text:
In 2023, 2024 and 2025 combined, 62,698 marriages were contracted where the older spouse lived in Norway [C1].

result.question: Of the age groups less than 25 years, 25-39, 40-54, 55-66 and 67 years or older, which had the highest average monthly earnings for full-time employees in Norway in 2025?
result.text:
The **55 years or older** group had the highest average monthly earnings for full-time employees in 2025, at about NOK 71,785 [C1] [E4].

The table reports finer age bands, so I combined them into your groups by taking the unweighted mean of the bands' averages:

| Age group | Average monthly earnings |
|---|---|
| Under 25 years | NOK 40,440 [C1] [E4] |
| 25–39 years | NOK 59,197 [C1] [E4] |
| 40–54 years | NOK 69,810 [C1] [E4] |
| 55 years or older | NOK 71,785 [C1] [E4] |

Notes: the figures are for 2025 and come from table 11421, "Monthly earnings, by measuring method, sector, industry, age, sex, contractual working hours and year", last updated 5 February 2026, covering all sectors and all industries, both sexes, full-time employees [E4]. The table's age bands are 0-24, 25-29, 30-34, 35-39, 40-44, 45-49, 50-54, 55-59 and 60 years or older [E4], so the oldest group here is the mean of the 55-59 band (NOK 71,890) and the open-ended 60+ band (NOK 71,680) [C1] [E4]. The group means are simple averages of band averages, not averages weighted by the number of employees in each band.

result.question: Hvorfor falt konsumprisindeksen fra 2024 til 2025, og med hvor mange prosent?
result.text:
Konsumprisindeksen falt ikke fra 2024 til 2025 – den steg. Årsendringen var 3,0 prosent i 2025, mot 3,2 prosent i 2024, altså en endring i prisveksten på −0,2 prosentpoeng [C1] [E3]. Indeksen (2025=100) var 97,1 i 2024 og 100 i 2025 [E3].

Prisveksten avtok altså, men prisene gikk opp også i 2025. Bak den lavere veksten lå særlig disse gruppene [E3]:

- Klær og skotøy: −2,2 prosent i 2025, mot 2,3 prosent i 2024 [E3].
- Drivstoff og smøremidler: −3,3 prosent i 2025, mot 0,4 prosent i 2024 [E3].
- Informasjon og kommunikasjon: 1,8 prosent i 2025, mot 2,2 prosent i 2024 [E3].

Samtidig trakk flere grupper opp [E3]:

- Bolig, elektrisitet og brensel: 4,0 prosent i 2025, mot 2,3 prosent i 2024; elektrisitet inkludert nettleie gikk fra −9,8 prosent i 2024 til 5,9 prosent i 2025 [E3].
- Forsikring og finansielle tjenester: 7,2 prosent i 2025, mot 4,0 prosent i 2024 [E3].
- Matvarer og alkoholfrie drikkevarer: 5,6 prosent i 2025, mot 5,3 prosent i 2024 [E3].

Tabellen har referanseår 2025=100, og endringstall beregnet fra denne serien kan avvike noe fra tall publisert tidligere med annet referanseår, hovedsakelig på grunn av avrunding [E3].

result.question: Reported offences in Norway doubled from 2015 to 2025. How many were reported in 2025?
result.text:
In 2025, 348,508 offences were reported to the police in Norway [E4].

The premise of the question is not supported by the figures: the number of reported offences did not rise from 2015 to 2025. In 2015 the total was 351,459 [E4], and the change from 2015 to 2025 was -0.8 per cent [C1].

Source: table 08484 "Offences reported to the police, by type of offence and year", all groups of offences, last updated 10 June 2026 [E4].

result.question: The GDP of Mainland Norway shrank in volume in 2025. By how many per cent?
result.text:
The premise is wrong: Mainland Norway's GDP did not shrink in 2025 — it grew [E8].

The volume change in GDP for Mainland Norway, at market values, was **1.7 per cent** in 2025 [E8]. In constant 2023 prices, the level rose from 4,047,656 million NOK in 2024 to 4,117,384 million NOK in 2025 [E8].

For context, the volume change was 0.9 per cent in 2023 and 0.6 per cent in 2024 [E8]. Figures after 2023, the base year, are preliminary [E8].
